name: Mortar
overview: Scripture presents mortar both as a practical material and a figurative symbol. It was used as a binding cement in construction, as seen in the building of the tower of Babel where slime served as mortar (Genesis 11:3), and for plastering houses (Leviticus 14:42). Mortar also appears as an instrument for grinding or pulverizing grain (Numbers 11:8), demonstrating its role in daily life. Figuratively, mortar illustrates the stubbornness of folly, as Proverbs 27:22 compares braying a fool in a mortar to the futility of removing foolishness. Additionally, the Scriptures depict mortar as untempered and fragile when improperly used, requiring firm treading to endure, highlighting the need for strength and stability.
